claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively coarse-grained microstructure.
Rapid thermal annealing at approximately 700°C for 30–60 seconds in an inert atmosphere will refine the coating to a sub-micron grain size.
Sub-micron grain refinement increases grain-boundary density.
The increased grain-boundary density hinders dislocation motion.
The refined grain structure delays crack nucleation.
The refined grain structure delays crack propagation.
Hindering dislocation motion and delaying cracking improves wear resistance during sliding.
Hindering dislocation motion and delaying cracking limits microscopic localized plastic deformation during sliding.
The annealed coating will exhibit less material removal than the as-deposited coating.
The annealed coating will exhibit less localized plastic deformation than the as-deposited coating.
The predicted wear and deformation improvements should hold during sliding in air at 500–700°C.
At temperatures significantly above 700°C, excessive grain growth could undermine the benefits of the refined microstructure.
The refined sub-micron grain structure may not persist during prolonged high-temperature sliding.
Dynamic recrystallization during extended service may reduce the benefits attributed to the refined microstructure.
A lack of statistically significant reductions in both wear rate and localized plastic deformation in the annealed samples would falsify the hypothesis.
